### Introduction:

The following exercise utilizes data from [UC Irvine Machine Learning Repository](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/datasets/Auto+MPG)

### Step 1. Import the necessary libraries

```{r step1, message=FALSE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
```

### Step 2. Import the first dataset [cars1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guipsamora/pandas_exercises/master/05_Merge/Auto_MPG/cars1.csv) and [cars2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guipsamora/pandas_exercises/master/05_Merge/Auto_MPG/cars2.csv).

### Step 3. Assign each to a variable called cars1 and cars2

```{r}
# the same files are also included in this folder: read_csv("cars1.csv"), read_csv("cars2.csv")
cars1 <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guipsamora/pandas_exercises/master/05_Merge/Auto_MPG/cars1.csv")
cars2 <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guipsamora/pandas_exercises/master/05_Merge/Auto_MPG/cars2.csv")

head(cars1)
head(cars2)
```

### Step 4. Oops, it seems our first dataset has some unnamed blank columns, fix cars1

```{r}
cars1 <- cars1 |> select(mpg:car)
head(cars1)
```

### Step 5. What is the number of observations in each dataset?

```{r}
dim(cars1)
dim(cars2)
```

### Step 6. Join cars1 and cars2 into a single DataFrame called cars

```{r}
# horsepower contains "?" for missing values in cars1, so it was read as text.
# bind_rows() needs the same type in both tables.
class(cars1$horsepower)
class(cars2$horsepower)

cars <- bind_rows(
  cars1 |> mutate(horsepower = as.character(horsepower)),
  cars2 |> mutate(horsepower = as.character(horsepower))
)
cars
```

### Step 7. Oops, there is a column missing, called owners. Create a random number vector from 15,000 to 73,000.

```{r}
nr_owners <- sample(15000:73000, size = nrow(cars), replace = TRUE)
head(nr_owners)
```

### Step 8. Add the column owners to cars

```{r}
cars <- cars |> mutate(owners = nr_owners)
tail(cars)
```
